title: Observer’s guide for ISO 2026-W05
planetary_coordinate: geocentric tropical ecliptic longitude; Monday 00:00 UTC

planet_relations.basis: Star Almanack preserved geocentric tropical ecliptic longitude
Star Almanack preserved geocentric tropical ecliptic longitude

note:
ISO 2026-W05 runs from January 26 through February 1. Mercury and Venus are separated by about 1.6° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn and Neptune are separated by about 1.9° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** No principal lunar phase is listed this week. Check the Moon's position each night and favor darker hours for low-contrast targets. Use Mintaka, Arneb, Alnilam, Phact, Alnitak, Saiph, Wazn, Betelgeuse, Menkalinan as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Mercury and Venus are separated by about 1.6° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Saturn and Neptune are separated by about 1.9° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** Favor β Dor, β Pic; wide fields help connect the charted geometry to the real sky.

**Small telescope:** Concentrate on Crab Nebula, Great Nebula in Orion, De Mairan's Nebula, M36, M78, M37. Increase magnification only after the target and surrounding pattern are secure.

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.
